plan: To prioritize capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This significantly reduces overall leverage and high-beta exposure.
The plan aims for a large cash buffer and focuses on broad index and income for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a substantial cash buffer. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to reduce overall leverage and meet the combined limit.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name concentration mandate.
This plan balances broad index exposure with quality tech and a small, controlled amount of leverage.
Aims for risk-first growth while maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: The balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, aiming for a more stable growth trajectory. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns compared to aggressive modes.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Add to METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, and SPAL, leveraging existing positions that are not flagged for sale or below stop.
This plan leans into higher-beta and leveraged ETFs for aggressive growth.
It maintains a smaller cash buffer and uses wider but strict stops to manage risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which amplifies both potential gains and losses. Be aware of higher drawdown risk and the daily decay/rebalancing effects of leveraged products; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions.
It aims for low drawdown and reliable income over growth, maintaining a cash buffer.
income.read: The income plan targets ~1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
